{{nihongo|'''Ōkawakami Birafu Shrine'''|大川上美良布神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tosa Province]].

'''Ōkawakami Birafu Shrine''' (おおかわかみびらふじんじゃ)<ref>In 'Kōchi-ken no Rekishi Sanpo,' the name is given simply as "Birafu Shrine," with "Ōkawakami" described as an honorific title. The torii plaque and Kōchi Prefecture cultural property registration use "Ōkawakami Birafu Shrine," the haiden plaque reads "Shō-ichii Birafu Shrine," and the information board reads "Shō-ichii Ōkawakami Birafu Shrine."</ref> is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Kahoku, Kōchi|Q11667146|qid=Q11667146}}, {{ill|Kami, Kōchi|Q877689|qid=Q877689}}, {{ill|Kōchi Prefecture|Q134093|qid=Q134093}}. It is an {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki-listed shrine}}, and its {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine rank}} was {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=kensha|qid=Q90139226}}.

The shrine buildings are adorned with exquisite carvings by master craftsmen, and at the time of their construction the shrine was called "{{ill|Tosa Province|Q857330|qid=Q857330|lt=Tosa}} {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|ar|ضريح توشوغو في نيكو|ca|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|cs|Nikkó Tóšógú|de|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|eo|Nikko Toŝo-gu|es|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|eu|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|fa|نیکو توشوگو|fr|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|id|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|it|Santuario di Nikko|ja|日光東照宮|ko|닛코 동조궁|ml|നിക്കൊ ടൊഷൊ-ഗു|nl|Nikko Toshogu|pl|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|pt|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|ru|Никко Тосё-гу|simple|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|th|ศาลเจ้านิกโกโทโช|tr|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|uk|Святилище Тосьо|zh|日光東照宮|qid=Q696641|lt=Nikkō}}."

===Overview===
The shrine is located approximately 100 meters north of the traffic signal in front of {{ill|Roadside station Birafu|Q11641461|qid=Q11641461}} along {{ill|Japan National Route 195|Q6156911|qid=Q6156911}}. "Birafu" (びらふ), which gives the shrine its name, can also be read as "mira," an archaic word for {{ill|Allium tuberosum|Q42285|qid=Q42285}}. The local place name is Nirōno (にろうの), and "nirō" can also be read as "nirafu," sharing the same meaning as "birafu."

The shrine's founding is said to date to the reign of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Q357235|qid=Q357235}}, though this remains in the realm of tradition. According to old records, there are descriptions indicating the shrine existed before {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} 8 ({{ill|841|Q24870|qid=Q24870}}) in the early {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}. The '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}},' compiled in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), also lists the shrine as one of four minor shrines in {{ill|Tosa Province|Q857330|qid=Q857330}} {{ill|Kami District, Kōchi|Q11667715|qid=Q11667715}}.

In antiquity, the shrine was also called "Kawakami Daimyōjin" or "Ōkawakamigū," and served as the sōchinju (head tutelary shrine) of the 50 villages of Nirō-gō. At the end of the {{ill|Bakumatsu|Q804558|qid=Q804558}} period, on {{ill|December 2 (Lunisolar)|Q840458|qid=Q840458|lt=the 2nd day of the 12th month}} of {{ill|Kaei|Q1146125|qid=Q1146125}} 5 ({{ill|January 11|Q2247|qid=Q2247}}, {{ill|1853|Q7666|qid=Q7666}}), the shrine received by imperial decree the highest {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} of Shō-ichii (Senior First Rank).

In the precinct stands a giant {{ill|Cryptomeria|Q147388|qid=Q147388|lt=cryptomeria}} tree said to be 1,000 years old, designated as the sacred tree. Its height is approximately 40 meters.

===Autumn Grand Festival===
Held annually over two days from November 2 to 3.

A sacred procession called "onabare," designated as a Kōchi Prefecture Intangible Folk Cultural Property, takes place. During the onabare, events include bō-uchi (stick fighting), goban-furi (go-board shaking), a portable-shrine procession, noses-on-stilts characters (hanadaka), a children's procession (chigo gyōretsu), and torimō/haguma (feathered poles approximately 5 meters tall adorned with bird feathers and fur). Within the precinct, there is a tsūyaden (night-vigil hall) containing an indoor revolving stage, and since {{ill|Enkyō (Edo period)|Q1183728|qid=Q1183728}} 4 ({{ill|1747|Q7596|qid=Q7596}}) during the mid-{{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}, {{ill|Kyōgen|Q944671|qid=Q944671}} performances have been staged there annually.

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Important Art Objects (nationally recognized) ===
*{{ill|Kesadasuki-mon bronze bells / unearthed at Nirōno, Birafu Village, Kami District, Kōchi Prefecture|Q48752055|qid=Q48752055}}
:Two {{ill|Dōtaku|Q2312868|qid=Q2312868}} (bronze bells) measuring 75.7 {{ill|Centimetre|Q174728|qid=Q174728|lt=cm}} and 67 cm in height. They were unearthed in the former Ioroi Village in the western part of Kahoku-chō and are said to have been dedicated to this shrine as sacred treasures. Known as the "Nirō no Furigane" (Falling Bells of Nirō), they were reportedly used in rain-invocation rituals at the {{ill|Monobe River|Q11570692|qid=Q11570692}}. Recognized on {{ill|September 1|Q2859|qid=Q2859}}, {{ill|1934|Q18714|qid=Q18714}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|ar|فترة شووا|br|Oadvezh Shōwa|ca|Període Shōwa|cs|Období Šówa|de|Shōwa-Zeit|eo|Ŝova-epoko|es|Era Shōwa|eu|Shōwa aroa|fa|دوره شووا|fi|Shōwa-kausi|fr|Ère Shōwa (1926-1989)|he|תקופת שווה|hi|शोवा युग|hu|Sóva-kor|id|Zaman Shōwa|it|Periodo Shōwa|ja|昭和|ka|შოვას პერიოდი|ko|쇼와 시대|lt|Šiova laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Shōwa|nl|Showaperiode|no|Shōwa-perioden|pl|Shōwa|pt|Período Shōwa|ru|Сёва|simple|Shōwa era|sr|Шова период|sv|Shōwa|th|ยุคโชวะ|tl|Panahong Shōwa|tr|Şova Dönemi|uk|Період Сьова|vi|Thời kỳ Chiêu Hòa|zh|昭和|zh_classical|昭和|zh_min_nan|Chiau-hô|zh_yue|昭和|qid=Q327567}} 9)<ref name="monbukokuji">{{Cite wikisource|和書|title=Recognition of Objects Related to the Preservation of Important Art Objects|wslink= 重要美術品等ノ保存ニ関スル物件認定_(昭和9年文部省告示第245号)|author=Ministry of Education Notification No. 245 of 1934|date=September 1, 1934|wslanguage=ja}}</ref>.

=== Kōchi Prefecture designated cultural properties ===
* Tangible cultural properties
**Shrine buildings
**: The haiden, heiden, and honden were begun in {{ill|Keiō|Q776775|qid=Q776775}} 1 ({{ill|1865|Q7708|qid=Q7708}}) and completed in {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 2 ({{ill|1869|Q7720|qid=Q7720}}). They feature chidori-hafu (cusped gables) and kara-hafu (undulating gables) for visual variation. Originally roofed with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=kokerabuki}} (thin wooden shingles), the roofs were replaced with copper sheeting in {{ill|1971|Q2475|qid=Q2475}} (Shōwa 46). Under master carpenter Shimamura Yasutaka, four carpenters competed against one another in their work. On the front center of the honden, Shimamura Yasutaka carved {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}}; Hara Uhei carved {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|Q1073668|qid=Q1073668}}; on the right, Sakaide Sadanosuke carved {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}}; and on the left, Betsuyaku Mokusaburō carved envoys from the {{ill|Samhan|Q1376093|qid=Q1376093}}. Other surfaces are also carved with scenes from {{ill|Japan|Q17|qid=Q17}}ese and {{ill|China (region)|als|China|ang|Cina|ar|الصين (منطقة)|arc|ܨܝܢ (ܐܪܥܐ)|ay|China|bat_smg|Kėnėjė (šalės)|bo|ཀྲུང་ཧྭ|br|Sina|ca|Xina|cdo|Dṳ̆ng-guók (dê-kṳ̆)|ckb|چین (ھەرێم)|cy|Tsieina|de|China|dz|རྒྱ་ནག|eo|Ĉinio (regiono)|es|China (región)|et|Hiina (maa)|eu|Txinaren izenak|fa|ملت چین|fiu_vro|Hiina|frp|Ch·ina|ga|An tSín|gan|中國|gd|Sìona (roinn chultarach)|gl|China (rexión)|gv|Yn Çheen Vooar|hak|Chûng-koet (thi-khî)|he|סין (אזור)|hi|चीन|id|Tiongkok (istilah)|is|Kína (menningarsvæði)|ja|中国|jam|Chaina|jv|Cina|kn|ಚೀನಾ|ko|중국|krc|Къытай (тарих регион)|ksh|China|kw|China|la|Sinae (regio)|lt|Kinija (regionas)|lv|Ķīna (reģions)|ml|ചൈനീസ് സംസ്കാരം|ms|China (kawasan)|nl|China|nn|Kina-regionen|no|Kina (kulturområde)|nrm|Chinne|pcd|Kine|pfl|China|pl|Chiny (region)|qu|Hatun Chinusuyu|ro|China (regiune)|rue|Китай|sa|चीनः (क्षेत्रम्)|sco|Cheenae (region)|simple|China|sk|Čína (civilizácia)|sl|Kitajska|sr|Кина (регион)|su|Tiongkok (istilah)|sv|Kina (region)|syl|ꠌꠣꠄꠘꠣ|ta|சீனா (பக்கவழி நெறிப்படுத்துதல்)|tpi|Saina (kainkain mining)|tr|Çin (bölge)|ug|جۇڭخۇا|uk|Китай|vi|Trung Quốc (khu vực)|war|Tsina|wuu|中国|yo|Ṣáínà|za|Cunghgoz (digih)|zh|中國|zh_classical|中國|zh_min_nan|Tiong-kok (iōng-gí)|zh_yue|中國|qid=Q29520|lt=Chinese}} {{ill|Chinese proverbs|Q1210892|qid=Q1210892}}.
